the_ruling_verbatim: her gate should admit her, fix it
now_the_spec_says: codemother's own charter admits codemother: gated_by becomes [codemother, CC]. An owner who cannot cross a boat at her own address owns nothing there, and the first boat she could not cross was her own component.
context: Raised as a finding of voyage 8754ae677af6 (codemother crosses a boat through the harbor door as herself). The build gave her a hand — 'cairn codemother cross <ticket> <target>' fires the harbor door with actor=codemother — and the voyage then could not use it on itself: cairn/devices/codemother/intention+why.json carried gated_by ['CC'], so the crossing that gave her a gate had to be made by CC. Reported to him as a spec choice at his gate rather than fixed on my own read; he ruled in six words. The shape is not novel — ['codemother','CC'] already stands at three other addresses in the corpus — so this is bringing her own address into line with the addresses she already gates, not inventing a permission. CC stays on the list: he did not rule CC off it, and removing a gate nobody asked to remove is exactly the widening a ruling is supposed to bound. Not confirmed: his words carry no RULED marker, so this packet is MY READING on the record, which is the door's designed resting state for an unmarked ruling and is never raised again.
